children.text: A block of mass \(m\) is attached to an ideal spring of constant \(k\). The other end is driven right at speed \(u\). Floor friction coefficients satisfy \(\mu_k<\mu_s\). Let \(x\) be spring elongation, \(x_k=\mu_kmg/k\), and \(\omega_0=\sqrt{k/m}\). Pure slip has kinetic friction throughout. Stick-slip alternates static and kinetic friction and can create creaking pulses.

nodes.alt: Original block attached to a spring whose end moves at speed u, with static and kinetic floor friction.

children.text: Initially the block slides at speed \(0<v_0<u\) and \(x(0)=x_k\). Find the period and elongation amplitude.
Now start the block at rest, still with \(x(0)=x_k\). Sketch laboratory velocity \(v(t)\) for three periods, and mark \(v=u\).
For the initial conditions of b, find long-time mean elongation.

Suppose the oscillation amplitude loses a small fraction \(\eta\ll1\) per pure-slip period through additional spring dissipation. Find the critical speed above which periodic stick-slip is impossible.

children.text: A door hinge is a thin hollow open-ended cylinder of radius \(r\), height \(h\) and thickness \(\Delta r\ll r\), pressing on its base with the weight of the whole door, mass \(M\). Its upper end turns with the rigid door, while its lower rim sticks. For shear angle \(\alpha\), \(dF=G\alpha\,dS\). Find torsional coefficient \(\kappa=\tau/\theta\). Use \(r=5\,\mathrm{mm}\), \(h=3\,\mathrm{cm}\), \(\Delta r=1\,\mathrm{mm}\), \(G=8\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{Pa}\).

Use \(\mu_s=0.75\), \(\mu_k=0.55\), \(M=30\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\). For slow opening, find the angular speed giving 20 Hz sound pulses. Assume the pure-slip oscillation frequency is much greater than 20 Hz. Give a formula and numerical value.

statement.text:
Creaking Door
A block of mass \(m\) is attached to an ideal spring of constant \(k\). The other end is driven right at speed \(u\). Floor friction coefficients satisfy \(\mu_k<\mu_s\). Let \(x\) be spring elongation, \(x_k=\mu_kmg/k\), and \(\omega_0=\sqrt{k/m}\). Pure slip has kinetic friction throughout. Stick-slip alternates static and kinetic friction and can create creaking pulses.

a1. Pure-slip period and amplitude
Initially the block slides at speed \(0<v_0<u\) and \(x(0)=x_k\). Find the period and elongation amplitude.
a2. Elongation sketch
Sketch \(x(t)\) for \(0<t<3T_0\).
b. Stick-slip velocity sketch
Now start the block at rest, still with \(x(0)=x_k\). Sketch laboratory velocity \(v(t)\) for three periods, and mark \(v=u\).
c. Mean elongation
For the initial conditions of b, find long-time mean elongation.
d. Stick-slip period
Find the new oscillation period.
e. Critical driving speed
Suppose the oscillation amplitude loses a small fraction \(\eta\ll1\) per pure-slip period through additional spring dissipation. Find the critical speed above which periodic stick-slip is impossible.
f. Hinge torsional stiffness

A door hinge is a thin hollow open-ended cylinder of radius \(r\), height \(h\) and thickness \(\Delta r\ll r\), pressing on its base with the weight of the whole door, mass \(M\). Its upper end turns with the rigid door, while its lower rim sticks. For shear angle \(\alpha\), \(dF=G\alpha\,dS\). Find torsional coefficient \(\kappa=\tau/\theta\). Use \(r=5\,\mathrm{mm}\), \(h=3\,\mathrm{cm}\), \(\Delta r=1\,\mathrm{mm}\), \(G=8\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{Pa}\).
g. Audible door speed
Use \(\mu_s=0.75\), \(\mu_k=0.55\), \(M=30\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\). For slow opening, find the angular speed giving 20 Hz sound pulses. Assume the pure-slip oscillation frequency is much greater than 20 Hz. Give a formula and numerical value.

children.text: Since \(\dot x=u-v\), the moving equation gives \(\ddot x+\omega_0^2(x-x_k)=0\). Thus \[T_0=2\pi\sqrt{m/k},\qquad A=(u-v_0)\sqrt{m/k}.\] The minimum block speed stays positive for the stated initial conditions.
\[x(t)=x_k+\frac{u-v_0}{\omega_0}\sin\omega_0t.\] Draw three sinusoidal periods about positive mean \(x_k\), starting at the mean with positive slope.

The block initially sticks while the elongation increases to \(x_s=\mu_smg/k\). It then slips in a sinusoidal positive hump and returns to zero velocity, followed by another stick interval. The mean velocity is u, so the humps exceed u. Their joins with the zero segments have discontinuous derivative.
In the frame of the driven end, the slip arc and uniform stick segment are symmetric about \(x_k\). Their mean displacement is zero, giving \(\overline x=\mu_kmg/k\).

Put \(q=(\mu_s-\mu_k)g\sqrt{m/k}/u\). The stuck distance in the driven frame is \(2(x_s-x_k)\), so \(t_{stick}=2(\mu_s-\mu_k)mg/(ku)\). The slipping phase misses angle \(2\arctan q\) of a full oscillator cycle. Therefore \[T=2\sqrt{m/k}\,[q+\pi-\arctan q].\]

At high drive speed, stick duration is short and \(\varphi\simeq(\mu_s-\mu_k)g\sqrt{m/k}/u\). The initial velocity amplitude in the driven frame is \(u/\cos\varphi\). To just avoid returning to zero lab velocity, it must decay to u in a cycle, so \(\eta=1-\cos\varphi\simeq\varphi^2/2\). Hence \[u_c=(\mu_s-\mu_k)g\sqrt{\frac{m}{2k\eta}}.\]

Top displacement is \(r\theta=h\alpha\). Torque on a base element is \(rG\alpha\,dS\), and base area is \(2\pi r\Delta r\). Thus \[\kappa=\frac{2\pi Gr^3\Delta r}{h}.\] The thin-wall estimate is about \(2.09\times10^3\,\mathrm{N\,m/rad}\).

Neglect slip duration. The twist accumulated per stick interval is \(\Delta\theta=2(\mu_s-\mu_k)Mgr/\kappa\). Therefore \[\Omega=f\Delta\theta=\frac{f(\mu_s-\mu_k)Mgh}{\pi Gr^2\Delta r}\simeq5.6\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{rad/s}.\] Finite-wall formulas are also defensible since \(\Delta r/r=0.2\) is not extremely small. The field uses the requested thin-wall approximation.

solution.text:
Creaking Door
a1. Pure-slip period and amplitude
Since \(\dot x=u-v\), the moving equation gives \(\ddot x+\omega_0^2(x-x_k)=0\). Thus \[T_0=2\pi\sqrt{m/k},\qquad A=(u-v_0)\sqrt{m/k}.\] The minimum block speed stays positive for the stated initial conditions.
a2. Elongation sketch
\[x(t)=x_k+\frac{u-v_0}{\omega_0}\sin\omega_0t.\] Draw three sinusoidal periods about positive mean \(x_k\), starting at the mean with positive slope.
b. Stick-slip velocity sketch
The block initially sticks while the elongation increases to \(x_s=\mu_smg/k\). It then slips in a sinusoidal positive hump and returns to zero velocity, followed by another stick interval. The mean velocity is u, so the humps exceed u. Their joins with the zero segments have discontinuous derivative.
c. Mean elongation
In the frame of the driven end, the slip arc and uniform stick segment are symmetric about \(x_k\). Their mean displacement is zero, giving \(\overline x=\mu_kmg/k\).
d. Stick-slip period
Put \(q=(\mu_s-\mu_k)g\sqrt{m/k}/u\). The stuck distance in the driven frame is \(2(x_s-x_k)\), so \(t_{stick}=2(\mu_s-\mu_k)mg/(ku)\). The slipping phase misses angle \(2\arctan q\) of a full oscillator cycle. Therefore \[T=2\sqrt{m/k}\,[q+\pi-\arctan q].\]
e. Critical driving speed
At high drive speed, stick duration is short and \(\varphi\simeq(\mu_s-\mu_k)g\sqrt{m/k}/u\). The initial velocity amplitude in the driven frame is \(u/\cos\varphi\). To just avoid returning to zero lab velocity, it must decay to u in a cycle, so \(\eta=1-\cos\varphi\simeq\varphi^2/2\). Hence \[u_c=(\mu_s-\mu_k)g\sqrt{\frac{m}{2k\eta}}.\]
f. Hinge torsional stiffness
Top displacement is \(r\theta=h\alpha\). Torque on a base element is \(rG\alpha\,dS\), and base area is \(2\pi r\Delta r\). Thus \[\kappa=\frac{2\pi Gr^3\Delta r}{h}.\] The thin-wall estimate is about \(2.09\times10^3\,\mathrm{N\,m/rad}\).
g. Audible door speed
Neglect slip duration. The twist accumulated per stick interval is \(\Delta\theta=2(\mu_s-\mu_k)Mgr/\kappa\). Therefore \[\Omega=f\Delta\theta=\frac{f(\mu_s-\mu_k)Mgh}{\pi Gr^2\Delta r}\simeq5.6\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{rad/s}.\] Finite-wall formulas are also defensible since \(\Delta r/r=0.2\) is not extremely small.
